Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Demand/Supply Chain Analyst, your resume and supporting documentation must support: A. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-12 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized.
MajorDuties: Conducting expert analysis regarding demand/supply chain performance issues and when required coordinating with functional process analysts and subject-matter specialists throughout the enterprise.
Utilizing available Information Technology (IT) systems to extract and analyze transactional data from IT systems of record and related data warehouses, tables, and resources.
Analyzing data regarding past, present, and projected demand/supply chain activity.

Evaluating implementation of accepted proposals for improving Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), metrics, and other demand/supply chain performance critical data to ensure the demand/supply chain area is meeting its performance targets.
Identifying trends and other factors adversely affecting performance and recommending improvements based on analyses and trends.
Advising and assisting senior management and enterprise Leadership in defining performance.

Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Management Analyst in the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) within the Business Office, Business Analysis Department of NAV FACILITIES ENGINEERING COMMAND SE.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will conduct detailed, comprehensive studies across various Command business lines to identify and establish the most efficient, cost-effective organizational structures and workflows throughout all phases of NAVFAC operations.

You will design and evaluate systematic process improvement initiatives engineered to increase overall productivity, elevate service quality, reduce operational costs, optimize staffing levels, and establish measurable performance milestones.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the (GS-07) grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: (1) Applying practical knowledge of ground support equipment (GSE) functions and management of assigned Integrated Product Team (IPT) hazardous waste containment and disposal program; (2) Identifying and scheduling ground support equipment for preventive maintenance and calibration to perform daily prerecords on ground support equipment and hazardous materials in accordance with policy/guidance; (3) Participating in the preventive maintenance planning, development, coordination, improvement, and implementation of procedures governing preventive maintenance of ground support equipment necessary to the mission of the agency; (4) Coordinating and managing assigned Integrated Product Team hazardous waste while ensuring compliance with agency policy and federal, state, and local hazardous waste and air emission rules and regulations; and (5) Acting as the calibration representative for the assigned area to ensure assets are turned before calibration expires, while overseeing all calibration support equipment on reports/documents. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Maintenance Management Specialist in the MRO Production Department of FLEET READINESS CENTER SOUTHWEST.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will analyze and review a variety of standard management reports such as aircraft schedules, materials lists, and calibration reports to develop a plan that supports Integrated Product Team operations.
You will conduct meetings and briefings to discuss problems and arrive at agreement on solutions or to inform or make recommendations to management.
You will use statistical methods such as trends and forecasts for developing graphs and charts to reflect discrepancies in planned ground support equipment (GSE) maintenance programs.

You will ensure all hazardous waste containers are properly labeled and in good condition, as well as accumulation sites are set up and maintained in accordance with the rules provided by the environmental office.
You will confirm all calibrated tools and equipment meet calibration due dates and to also coordinate this effort with artisans and calibration personnel.

You will coordinate special projects with other Integrated Product Teams to help analyze ground support equipment preventive maintenance, man-hours, and cost versus projections and assets to indicate significant deviations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Resume must reflect the experience as a professional mariner that demonstrates a mastery of all aspects of the art and sciences of navigation, seamanship, and ship handling, in order to make decisions and recommendations significantly shaping Fleet training and SWSC policies. This position requires the incumbent to be an experienced, former U.S. Navy Officer or equivalent who has had Command of two or more surface combatants or one surface combatant and command of a Destroyer Squadron or equivalent with significant knowledge of navigation, seamanship, and ship handling principles, where this broad base of experience has prepared the incumbent to be able to teach, advise and mentor on all aspects of navigation, seamanship, and ship handling, including assessing student competencies in accordance with applicable guidance. 2) Resume must show extensive in-depth knowledge and experience utilizing bridge simulator/trainers, or similar ship handling simulators/trainers, understanding its operation, capabilities, and limitations, understanding advance ship handling principles, and U.S. Navy surface ship particulars and maneuvering characteristics of all U.S. Navy -ship classes. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). You will instruct Surface Division Officers, Department Heads, Executive Officers, Commanding Officers, and Major Commanders on navigation, seamanship and ship handling.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-11) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience exhibits substantial skill in applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques by gaining information/facts, organizing, and writing reports that set forth an unbiased and realistic position of the subject under consideration for optimum analysis and decision making. Must be able to relate aspects and parts of a project to the overall needs of the organization in order to accomplish projects. Must exercise initiative and sound judgment and possess ability to plan, devise, and formulate work procedures and methods to meet requirements for the command and its customers. Thorough knowledge of documentation and reports preparation to generate items as needed for the command. Knowledge in the area of data collection, collation, organization, and presentation in the form of written and oral reports, charts, graphs, videos, multimedia presentations, or other format as appropriate to meet specific documentation requirements for the command and its customers. Must have a good working knowledge of the Defense Travel System (DTS) and current travel regulations, along with the ability to review, interpret, and apply changing policies to ensure the command travel program is in compliance. Must have a broad knowledge of mid-level computing applications such as word processing and spreadsheets, specifically, Microsoft Office products as applications are regularly used for analysis, documentation and tracking purposes. Must have a basic knowledge of structure and work processes involved in other subsystems (e.g. supply, financial, contracting) so as to recognize possible conflicts. Must have the ability to write procedural flow charts to document requirements. Must have a general knowledge of supply regulations, policies, documentation, and procedures and must have a good working knowledge of the command's products and services and their interactions with financial functions. Must have the ability to study and comprehend complex matrix organizations along with their associated interrelationships within the command and with other activities, and their funding sources in order to plan, analyst and establish mission and reimbursable funding requirements and budgets. General knowledge of civilian and military personnel structures, schedules, ranks, reports and pay scales to locate information required in determining budgets, forecasting expenditures, calculating labor cost increases or reductions, and understanding manning requirements. Knowledge of and skill in applying the NAVSUPINST 4205.3E series as COR to ensure compliance when serving as contract COR. Skill in monitoring contracts to ensure compliance with the Statement of Work, contract schedules, and contract expenditures. Ability to serve as technical liaison between the Government and the contractor. Must have the ability to study procedures, policies, documentation, reports, tables, charts, graphs, and automated systems in order to understand their relation to financial systems and procedures. Must have the knowledge of Navy correspondence, including letters, memorandums, email and other forms of communications to ensure compliance when generating documentation requirements. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for the GS-14 grade level, your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Extensive operational experience managing and delivering comprehensive training continuums for Maritime Operations Centers (MOCs) or equivalent major fleet/combatant command staff, which includes developing training plans, collection management plans (CMPs), facilitated after-action reviews (FAAR), and MOC certification reports (MCRs). Experience demonstrating leadership and project management skills to provide technical oversight and pre-deployment coordination for a diverse team of 25-30 Observer/Trainers (O/Ts) and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), including active duty and reserve military (O-4 to O-6), government civilians, and contractors, during large-scale service and Combatant Commander (CCDR) exercises. Experience utilizing oral and written communication skills required to deliver high-level briefs, represent organizational equities in joint decision-making forums, and interact routinely with Flag/General Officers, Senior Executive Service (SES) members, Fleet Commanders, and other senior joint, interagency, and international leadership. Experience applying knowledge of the Navy Maritime Operations Center (MOC) operational construct and the seven joint functions (movement and maneuver, command and control, fires, intelligence, information operations, protection, and sustainment) to critically assess MOC readiness and institutionalize global training standards. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Maritime Operations Center Training Analyst (IAMD) in the Training, Exercises, and Wargaming (N7) Department, Maritime Operations Center (MOC) Training and Exercise Division of the Navy Warfare Development Center.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as a desk officer on the Maritime Operations Center (MOC) Training and Exercise Team (TET).
You will be responsible for developing and executing the training plan to ensure standardization between fleet requirements and mission performance.
You will support the standardization of Navy operational-level of warfare (OLW) training and readiness reporting across the ten Navy MOCs.

You will coordinate with major and numbered fleet training officers and MOC leadership to deliver a comprehensive MOC training continuum composed of functional part-task training, team, and staff collective training to improve fleet readiness.
You will provide support and oversight of a facilitated-after action review (FAAR) upon exercise completion.
You will coordinate the delivery of training in the areas of force protection, operations security, force health protection, and other elements of Protection as a joint function.

You will develop and manage the content and organization of Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) and Protection-related topics for inclusion in the MOC Effective Practices Handbook and on the MOC TET portal.
You will represent Navy operational-level training equities in joint and other service forums and participate in the crafting of official Navy training strategies.
You will develop, plan, prepare, execute, and assess Navy training and exercises designed to train operational-level staffs in functional warfare competencies across the range of military operations.
You will perform other duties as assigned.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experienced and skilled in applying quantitative and qualitative analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to identify interrelated program problems, draw conclusions, and recommend appropriate action to improve mission effectiveness. Experience analyzing conflicting data and summarizing recommendations or program changes considering various points of view and specifying the reasons for choices. Experience and expert knowledge of pertinent laws, regulations, policies and precedents which affect the use of program and related support resources in DoD and Navy Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) and POM processes, as well as understanding of the methodologies of these processes and the associated goals and objectives of the processes sufficient to evaluate requirements and develop POM packages. Experience and comprehensive knowledge of service requirement development processes, to include concepts, science and technology, and experimentation. Experience and knowledge of the Navy resource allocation process sufficient to optimize resources among program elements to best satisfy the prioritized operational requirements of the assigned programs. Experience and the highest degree of interpersonal skills is required to articulate the command's requirements. Experience with intermediate (or above) level computer skills to include spreadsheet, database, graphics and word processing. Work requires the production of project papers, staff reports, and executive level correspondence. Must be able to apply mature judgment, have a high degree of initiative and be persistent with tact. Experience working multiple organization segments to meet program requirements and objectives within the available resources and having the ability to establish and prioritize work to meet fluctuating deadlines and respond to a variety of requirements and keep other work moving toward completion. Experience effectively communicating, orally and in writing, to produce final products for use by the Commander in presenting strategy, policy, planning, and operational issues. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Supervisory Program Analyst in the of NAVINFOWARDEVCEN NORFOLK.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will be responsible for leading the command’s doctrine development and validation process and executing the agile doctrine concept through the collaboration information environment.
You will oversee the collection and tracking of actions and recommendations gathered from exercises, experiments, deployment reports, studies, concept of operations and other sources.
You will develop and submit the command’s Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) efforts supporting the Naval Capability Development Process.
You will align operational requirements with appropriate resources, manpower, training and equipment.
You will review and approve work plans to be accomplished by subordinates, establish priorities, and schedule completion of work.
You will set broad objectives, monitor subordinate employees' performance in providing services, review accomplishments, and take appropriate corrective actions when deficiencies are noted.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service: Performing military operational planning, execution and force deployment operations processes for force deployment execution; Managing, analyzing and providing recommendation on force management requirements, status and courses of action to plan, organize and oversee study/projects and objectives, sequence and timing of key events and methods of evaluation; Providing visibility of forces in various stages of readiness while interacting with other senior level military offices/counterparts; and utilizing a wide range of program management policies, guidelines, and concepts to develop policy guidance use of joint forces. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for roles, responsibilities, processes, and tools associated with the sourcing, deployment tracking, employment, redeployment tracking and reconstitution/regenerations of emergent, and rotational forces to meet Combatant Commander's operational requirements..
Details.SubAgencyName: Regional Operations & Force Management (VDDJ35) Joint Force Coordination Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-3 (Operations), supports the Chairman in carrying out responsibilities as the principal military advisor to the President and Secretary of Defense, developing and providing guidance to the combatant commanders and relaying communications between the President and the Secretary of Defense and the combatant commanders regarding current operations and plans
MajorDuties: As a GLOBAL FORCE MANAGEMENT (GFM) ANALYST (AIR FORCE) at the GS-0301-12 some of your typical work assignments may include: Prepares and reviews weekly force tracking and readiness reports of major force elements and units that depict Air Force unit availability to meet combatant commander requirements. Retrieves data elements and transcribes this material into a visual representation to brief leadership within the Joint Staff regarding the status of military forces. Assists the Branch lead, which includes such tasks as verifying Service and Combatant Commander readiness issues to discern the validity and accuracy when applied to the Global Force Management Allocation plan. Reviews department documentation, preparation, and delivery of oral briefings with accompanying visual aids, draft e-mails for transmission by senior leadership, information papers, and analytical summary spreadsheets, data tables, and databases. Examines Force Provider negative responses in meeting a validated Combatant Commander requirement need, produces accurate inventory of the required force by accessing information technology systems, and reviews risk statements of the requestor and requested.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a COMMANDER'S ACTION GROUP ASSISTANT in the COMMANDER NAVAL INFORMATION WARFIGHTING DEVELOPMENT CENTER of NAVINFOWARDEVCEN NORFOLK. This is a RE-ADVERTISEMENT of Announcement Number: ST-13105622-27-EIF. Applicants that have previously applied NEED to re-apply to this announcement.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite! GS-11 = $ 75,788 - $ 98,530 GS-12 = $ 90,838 - $ 118,092
MajorDuties: You will serve as a key facilitator for coordinating staff actions and information requests involving the Commander, handling specialized, sensitive, and time-critical assignments.

You will interact regularly with directorate staff and external points of contact to enable command leadership by preparing administrative and operational communication products, addressing inquiries, and coordinating input across departments.
You will conduct preliminary reviews of reports, projects, and correspondence submitted to the Commander via the CAG lead, to ensure appropriate staff work and clear options or recommendations.
You will initiate, plan, and conduct staff studies and operational reviews to improve administrative efficiency, organizational workflows, or communication channels across functional boundaries.
You will gather and analyze information to develop recommendations for resolving operational bottlenecks or improving administrative support to the Commander.
You will organize and prepare finished written materials and supporting audiovisual presentations with general guidance.
You will represent the CAG in staff meetings and working groups to facilitate communications, gather data, and convey command preferences.

GS-11 Successful completion of a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree OR Successful completion of 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree OR Possession of an LL.M., if related A combination of experience and graduate education as described above that equates to one year of experience A transcript must be submitted with your application if qualifying using education. See Required Documents for additional information.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a GS-13, your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience applying subject matter expertise in all disciplines of Information Operations (IO)/Information Warfare (IW); information related capabilities (IRC), military strategic, theater and operational planning, and operational/tactical application to maximize the effectiveness of the Navy's IO/IW capability. Experience applying thorough knowledge of Joint planning procedures and policy; Counter Intelligence Concepts, principles and practices to orchestrate implementation of S/O plans; awareness of research and development (R&D) agencies, technologies and capabilities and the ability to incorporate into S/O plans; and appropriate legal and regulatory guidance used in planning and directing IO operations. Experience applying working knowledge of Joint and Fleet operational IO concepts and practices; counter-intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C-ISR) concepts, methodologies and techniques; foreign, friendly and hostile naval operational IO/IW concepts; operational employment of IO equipment, tactics and doctrine; as well as experience in and knowledge of the various physical science disciplines associated with the technological and tactical requirements of current and emerging IO capabilities and applications. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

You will review Naval and Joint IO/special technical operations (STO)/Cyberspace doctrine, policy, directives and instructions.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a MEDICAL PLANS and OPERATIONS OFFICER in the OFFICE OF THE FORCE SURGEON DIVISION of COMNAVSURFLANT.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as subject-matter-expert (SME) and technical expert with full responsibility for all activities involved in the management of operations, plans, programs and logistics in support of Commander, Naval Surface Force Atlantic (CNSL).

You will review the critical military medical capabilities required to support the operational Surface Force, analyze policy, and monitor compliance and effectiveness of military operational medical support.
You will apply Service and Joint medical doctrine through the continuum of care within the Surface Force.
You will work with experts in Service, Joint, and Defense Health Agency (DHA) Headquarters with a full comprehension of medical planning tools and data sources.
You will assist the Force Surgeon with performing analytically rigorous methodologies used in the development of current and future Joint operational medical force planning and modernization.
Details.Evaluations: In order to qualify for this position, your resume must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the specific position for which you are being considered. Your resume is the key means we have for evaluating your skills, knowledge, and abilities as they relate to this position. Therefore, we encourage you to be clear and specific when describing your experience. When the application process is complete, we will review your resume to ensure you meet the hiring eligibility and qualification requirements listed in this announcement. You will be rated based on the information provided in your resume and application package, along with your supporting documentation to determine your ability to demonstrate the following competencies: ADMINISTRATION AND MANAGEMENT BUSINESS OPERATIONS HUMAN CAPITAL MANAGEMENT PLANNING AND EVALUATING PROBLEM SOLVING STRATEGIC THINKING This recruitment will utilize the following technical assessment tools: Structured Resume Review, Structured Interview. You should list any relevant performance appraisals and incentive awards in your resume as that information may be taken into consideration during the selection process. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. If after reviewing your resume and supporting documentation, a determination is made that you inflated your qualifications and/or experience, your score may be adjusted to more accurately reflect your abilities or you may be found ineligible/not qualified. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. All eligibility, qualifications, and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference? If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Supplemental documents may contain your SSN, DOB, or personal information of others (e.g., on military orders, marriage certificates). You may redact this information before submitting; however, if selected, you must provide unredacted originals.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName: Immediate Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-XX) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate performing duties such as the following; 1. Translating operational capabilities and environments, and foreign threat insight into test capability requirements. 2. Submitting Requests for Information (RFIs) and tasking intelligence production centers for adversary TTPs and material advances. 3. Understanding of DOW intelligence oversight guidelines with desired expertise in managing organizational compliance to these directives. 4. Evaluating and accrediting physical targets, surrogate platforms (aerial, surface, undersea), electronic attack emitters, and cyber threat vectors to ensure they accurately represent threat behaviors and signatures. 5. Utilizing scientific, technical, and assessment expertise with underlying understanding of threat modeling and simulation, kinetic and non-kinetic threat capabilities, and emulation methods. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a MANAGEMENT AND PROGRAM ANALYST (STILO) within COMOPTEVFOR.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as the OPTEVFOR Scientific and Technical Intelligence Liaison Officer (STILO) in accordance with OPNAVINST 3880.6 (series), serving as the command’s primary point of contact for intelligence and threat-support requirements.

You will identify, translate, validate, prioritize, and communicate OPTEVFOR intelligence requirements; maintain awareness of command programs and projects; and disseminate applicable finished intelligence to support operational test and evaluation.

You will ensure threat assessments, threat data, threat models, and other intelligence used in OPTEVFOR OT and E are current, valid, and consistent with applicable intelligence positions, policies, and accreditation requirements.
You will facilitate OPTEVFOR access to Intelligence Community resources and coordinate intelligence support for OT and E, Fleet experimentation, and rapid capability development and fielding efforts.
You will participate in OT and E test design, planning, execution, and evaluation activities; coordinate Intelligence Community and Fleet N2 participation as appropriate.
You will ensure intelligence requirements are incorporated into test products, including Integrated Evaluation Frameworks, test plans, scenarios, and threat-representation validation activities.

You will maintain effective liaison among OPTEVFOR, OPNAV, the Office of Naval Intelligence, other STILOs, Fleet N2 organizations, Systems Commands, Warfare Centers, and Department of War and Intelligence Community partners.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience applying techniques of project management to include workflow, plant layout, time and engineered work standards, work simplification, safety. Experience exercising production control to include requisitioning, storage, delivery, inventory, and material handling. Experience applying extensive knowledge in the concepts, principles, and practices of ship repair planning, work execution, and performance monitoring as an authority on the planning and execution of ship overhaul or inactivation/recycling work. Experience evaluating the performance of projects through Advanced Industrial Management (AIM), Critical Path Method (CPM) Analysis, Performance Measurement and Control system (PMC), regulations concerning costing and other programs Experience exercising shipyard nuclear production trades operations, production planning and control, ship systems engineering, ship systems testing, material management, equipment, facilities, schedule control, quality control, budget and cost control, and safety practices and procedures. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SUPERVISORY PROJECT MANAGEMENT SPECIALIST (PS) in the Nuclear Productions Department, Code 300N of NORFOLK NAVAL SHIPYARD.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as a consultant and advisor to all levels of shipyard management relative to the feasibility of workload commitments and work schedule modifications on project availabilities.
You will establish and revise priorities and procedures for the operation of department components and programs.

You will define and assign work to subordinates functions and work operations in accordance with overall Nuclear Production Department workload and priorities and operations of personnel, and equipment required.
You will be responsible for shifting manpower and other operations resources to meet emergency work assignments.

You will review cost and work progress reports to anticipate and/or initiate corrective action prior to exceeding cost limits or failing to meet production schedules and ensuring only authorized work is undertaken.
You will schedule, coordinate and direct the accomplishment of work projects or operations by subordinate units through subordinate supervisors.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SUPERVISORY PROGRAM ANALYST in the PROJECT MANAGEMENT OFFICE in the WATERFRONT OPERATIONS DEPARTMENT of SOUTHWEST REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite! Headquartered at Pearl Harbor on the island of Oahu in Hawaii, this four-star command is the world's largest fleet command. Encompassing 100 million square miles, our 200 ships/submarines, nearly 1,200 aircraft, and more than 130,000 uniformed and civilian Sailors serve on nearly half of the Earth's surface -- from Antarctica to the Arctic Circle, and from the U.S. West Coast to the Indian Ocean. Join the USPACFLT team to achieve more and to help protect and defend the maritime interests of the U.S. in the Indo-Pacific, providing combat-ready forces and operating forward, ready to fight tonight. We want talent and enthusiasm aboard the USPACFLT team. We want the best! For further information, please visit https://www.cpf.navy.mil/.
MajorDuties: You will advise the Technical Director, Department Head, PMO Division Head, and other department leadership regarding the status of all current and proposed strategic department programs within the Waterfront Operations Department.
You will counsel, advise, coach and/or direct employees on technical and administrative projects.
You will develop employee performance elements and standards, evaluates work performance of subordinates, and provides recommended ratings of record.
You will use trend and historical analysis to ensure appropriate funding and budget levels are maintained and responsible expenditures are authorized.
You will be responsible for additional duties requiring organized management of division minor property assets, managing time certification and payroll issues.
You will design, adapt, revise, and evaluate operating reports, procedures, and operations encompassing multiple Waterfront Operations management systems.

You will analyze operating procedures to identify areas of potential non-compliance, explain discrepancies, and provide authoritative policy interpretation to ensure modification of existing operations.
You will review/analyze proposed policy changes to determine its impact on current operations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1 - Executive Multi-Level Supervision and Leadership: Experience as a second-level (or higher) supervisor with authority over subordinate GS-11/12 analysts. Evidence must include directing a large, geographically dispersed workforce, executing administrative/personnel functions (e.g., hiring, discipline, labor relations, performance evaluations), and implementing human capital strategies. 2 - Enterprise-Level Fleet Ordnance Program Management: Mastery of enterprise-wide Fleet Ordnance Support (FOS) programs. Experience must encompass direct operational oversight of retail ammunition management, including ordnance receipt, storage, segregation, and issue (RSSI); ordnance inventory management and accountability, ordnance on/off loading of specific Navy CVNs, DDGs, LCS and T-AKE ships. Experience with transshipment requirements via aircrafts and ships. 3 - Strategic Planning and Multi-Regional Governance: Ability to develop and direct strategic plans, policies, and operational priorities for a complex organization with multiple subordinate commands operating across different areas of responsibility (CONUS and OCONUS). Must demonstrate experience aligning resources and resolving conflicts across diverse fleet and shore-based stakeholders. 4 - Executive Stakeholder Relations and Negotiation: Experience representing an organization with echelon II and III commands that include 5th and 6th Fleet N4s, NAVEUR N4, and USFFC N4 representatives. Must have experience settling significant, often controversial, resource and policy matters. 5 - Comprehensive Business and Resource Management: Expertise in developing Program Objective Memorandum inputs that address the Fleet Ordnance Support mission requirements in the FYDP. 6 - High-Risk Program and Safety/Security Compliance: Experience overseeing operations in a high-risk environment involving explosives, industrial processes, and classified information. Must demonstrate knowledge of statutory and regulatory compliance for explosives safety, industrial safety, and physical/information security (SECRET clearance required). Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Supervisory Management & Program Analyst in the Navy Munitions Command Atlantic (NMCLANT), Ordnance Operations & Technical Support Det (N3/N4) of NMCLANT YORKTOWN VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will develop, monitor, and coordinate the execution of programs and procedures related to ammunition stock point and retail ammunition management, and inventory and storage operations management for NMCLANT and its subordinate activities.
You will establish standards for ordnance storage and supply management and monitors performance across the Command.
You will interpret Navy policy regarding supply and inventory management, develop implementing Command policies and procedures, and ensure that required procedures are adhered to.

You will develop user level processes and procedures for supported activities, taking into account the unique requirements of the stock point, the ashore and afloat customer base, and Fleet response and training plans.
You will monitor ordnance physical inventory management and accounting/accountability program performance by ordnance managers at NMCLANT subordinate activities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Cont. of Conditions of Employment This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions; Management and Program Analysis Series, 0343. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-11, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes extensive in-depth knowledge of the mission, organization and work processes of programs throughout a military command, and the relationships of administrative support activities to such missions. Knowledge is applied when assessing programs/projects, analyzing findings and making recommendations on substantive operating programs. The work requires skill in preparing staff reports/briefings and skill in organizing and delivering briefings to managers to encourage understanding and acceptance of findings and recommendations; Extensive knowledge of qualitative and quantitative techniques for analyzing and measuring effectiveness, efficiency and productivity of administrative and technical programs; Knowledge of military command structure, missions, programs, and organizational relationships and program goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones and methods of evaluating planning actions as they relate to actual events; Extensive knowledge of DoD and United States Air Force (USAF) strategic plans and strategic planning processes in order to develop short- and long-range planning guidance in accordance with USAF and command policies and objectives. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Expert knowledge of Joint operational-level and tactical-level command and control, as well as the applicable tactics, techniques and procedures for the specified domain, for application to assigned projects and events. Expert knowledge of the specified domain processes, procedures and TTPs as applied to assigned sensitive military capabilities, operations, weapons systems and relevant non-AF C2. Advanced ability to gather, assemble, and analyze facts, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, devise recommended solutions, and package the entire process in briefings, papers, or reports suitable for top management use and decision-making. Experience in leading the planning, execution and assessment of Joint Multi-Domain operations/ experiments/ tests/exercises, to include familiarity with the Joint Test Cycle (JTC) and/or the Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC), at the COCOM/MAJCOM level. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and staff of a small to medium sized organization. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. Air Force/Joint Electronic Warfare Officer and operations center experience required. Weapons School, Checkmate, and/or Contingency Warfare planner experience desired. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is: To serve as an Event Director, Event Analyst, and specified domain (Air/Space/Cyber/Land/Maritime/NKE-EW) Subject Matter Expert (SME) in the Shadow Operations Center-Nellis (ShOC-N) with the responsibility for providing both advanced expertise in the planning, execution and assessment of assigned technologies and events. DUTIES: Plans, organizes, and directs the activities of United States Air Force Warfare (USAFWC) Shadow Operations Center (ShOC-N) Battlelab in the 805th Combat Training Squadron (CTS) as a Multi-Domain Event Planner/Director. Will functionally and operationally assess JADC2/ABMS applications, software and TTPs for integration into ShOC-N supported or hosted events as event domain analyst. Apply EW/NKE domain subject matter expertise to multi-Domain scenario development, modeling and simulation execution and analysis in support of the organic Battlelab live, synthetic environment (LSE).

MajorDuties: GS-0301-07: 1. Services Program Administration: Performs a variety of administrative and operational duties to support the full spectrum of Base Services programs. Assists in managing the Food Service, Contingency Lodging, Fitness programs, Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs by tracking compliance, maintaining records, and preparing reports. Implements program policies at the direction of the supervisor, ensuring that day-to-day operations align with governing standards. Assists in the planning, coordination, and execution of MWR events to maximize base community participation. Gathers and compiles data for readiness reporting systems and helps maintain program continuity binders and operating instructions. Utilizes systems such as the Subsistence Total Order Requisition Electronic System (STORES) for managing food service requisitions. 2. Readiness and Deployment Support: Provides direct support to the flight's mobility and readiness program. Maintains personnel readiness folders, ensuring they are complete, accurate, and up to date. Assists in the deployment planning process by tracking personnel availability, training requirements, and equipment status. Coordinates with the unit deployment manager and other base agencies to ensure all pre-deployment requirements for tasked personnel are met in accordance with applicable personnel readiness instructions. Help prepare and maintain Prime Readiness in Base Services(RIBS) team kits and recall plans. 3. Financial and Logistical Support: Assists in the administration of the unit's financial and supply programs. Helps prepare purchase requests and supporting documentation for equipment, supplies, and services, including tracking food and subsistence expenditures via the STORES system. Monitors stock levels of consumables and supplies, initiating re-orders as needed to support training and operational requirements. Assists with maintaining accountability of equipment listed on the Custodian Authorization-Custody Receipt Listing (CA/CRL). Provides support for the administration of Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) by helping to maintain records and prepare required documentation as directed. As liaison for the Private Organization and Unofficial Activity programs, maintains official files and assists in the annual review of financial statements, governing documents, and other required records to ensure compliance with command policies. To qualify at the GS-12 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: Utilizing a wide range of analytical, statistical, and mathematical tools, and is responsible for defining the risks and the quantifiable relationship between the input and output variables Reviewing various performance metrics, identified risks within functional areas or distribution centers, as well as deficiencies to assist with identifying projects Conducting studies/projects, analyzing findings, making recommendations, and implementing recommendations using change management principles on substantive operating programs Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Frequent travel to facilities throughout the DLA Distribution network may be required.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: America's Combat Logistics Support Agency: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) agency. DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized. By joining Defense Logistics Agency Distribution, you will be a part of the team that is the leading provider of global distribution support to America's military. Whether you work at the DLA Distribution Headquarters in New Cumberland, PA or at one of our 24 distribution centers around the globe, your work will ensure that DLA Distribution offers the right solution, on time, every time through a broad range of services to include storage, distribution, customized kits, specialized packaging and world-wide transportation support. DLA Distribution makes a difference every day by providing effective, efficient and best value support to our customers which include the United States Army, Marine Corps, Navy and Air Force as well as other government agencies.
MajorDuties: Serves as DLA Distribution Lean Six Sigma (LSS) Continuous Process Improvement (CPI) project team analyst and member within Compliance, Financial Audit and Infrastructure Management (CFAIM) Directorate, Compliance Division

Identifies and improves productivity efficiencies and processes utilizing LSS and other CPI techniques and participates in the initiation, oversight, and organization of assigned projects and initiatives
Gathers, analyzes, and provides lean metrics to the Distribution CPI Project Team Officer
Reports risk mitigation strategy, tangible cost benefits and Return on Investment (ROI) results gained from implementation of processes
Identifies and recommends which tools, software, and training are required
Informs the supervisor of potentially controversial findings, issues, or problems with widespread impact
Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) evaluating distribution center leadership practices, process management, and performance management systems
Ability to coordinate multiple projects and align efforts of cross-dimensional stakeholders
Highlight and expand relationships between departments and identifying common goals
Ability to develop, execute and train others on proficiency associated with analytical data, execution andsustainment

The DoD criteria for hiring Reemployed Annuitants can be found at: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/140025/140025_vol300.PDF Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. MajorDuties: Its purpose is to serve as the Aircraft Maintenance Coordinator, with responsibility for the overall maintenance effort on the flightline to include work operations performed by two or more distinct organizational units and controlled by a number of separate supervisors. The position does not have supervisory duties or responsibilities. Responsible for the total squadron maintenance program, manages the overall direction of the maintenance effort, and enforces safe maintenance practices. In addition, responsible for identifying, assembling, and managing critical equipment items. Priority is placed on aircraft supporting operational requirements, scheduled and unscheduled aircraft maintenance, and aircraft used for maintenance and/or operations training. The focus is on aircraft generation in order to meet mission requirements. Incumbent has maintenance authority on airworthiness of aircraft based on knowledge of aircraft systems and safety of flight concerns. Ensures that a pilot pickup is accomplished for critical parts in order to expedite repairs of Not-Mission-Capable aircraft that receive the highest priority and depends on the critical need for the aircraft and its return to service. May verify Mission Capable (MICAP) requisitions. Participates in establishing the monthly and weekly maintenance plans. Attends the daily maintenance planning meetings for the purpose of incorporating unscheduled maintenance into the weekly and daily maintenance plans. Evaluates workload requirements and makes changes to aircraft utilization schedules as required. Takes prompt and decisive action to make on-the-spot adjustments to maintenance repair priorities necessitated by unscheduled maintenance requirements. Controls and coordinates maintenance activity on the flightline. Monitors aircraft maintenance in progress and evaluates estimated completion time against scheduling and planning requirements. Anticipates problems and directs changes of flightline activities in order to meet mission schedules. May be required to coordinate with supervisors to select workers and assign tasks to be performed. When necessary, initiates action to resolve personnel shortages and coordinates requirements with the Maintenance Operations Center (MOC). Reviews work in progress or upon completion for compliance with policies and procedures. Ensures utilization of proper tools and equipment and adherence to technical data in performance of maintenance. Determines methods necessary to meet mission requirements including authorizing and directing cannibalization on assigned aircraft. Cannibalization actions will be coordinated with the MOC and Supply. Ensures aircraft status is accurately reported in accordance with Air Force instructions, reports, and applicable supplements. Works closely with the expediter and MOC to ensure that actual aircraft status matches the aircraft status reported in the automated reporting system. Understands, executes, and coordinates specific disaster control duties including the provisions contained Air Force instructions, with regard to movement of aircraft, support equipment, and evacuation of flightline personnel. Decisions will be made based on safeguarding personnel first, followed by protecting aircraft, equipment, and other resources. Maintains a current on-base disaster map with cordon overlay and appropriate checklists for use during disasters or exercises.

This position is responsible for the control and accomplishment of management functions associated with the administration, management, operation and utilization of facilities and assets.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: CNIC offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. CNIC provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. The mission of the Fleet and Family Readiness (FFR) Programs is to maximize the physical, emotional and social development of the fleet, fighter and family. FFR enables a ready Navy force through its Fleet Readiness, Family Readiness, and Housing Programs. We provide direct and support services to all non-appropriated fund (NAF) employees who work for Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR), and Navy Getaways throughout the FFR Program worldwide.
MajorDuties: The incumbent directs and oversees the daily activities and overall operations of a full-service club. Responsibilities include ensuring the effective delivery of food and beverage services, social activities, and entertainment programs for authorized patrons and their guests. Establishes and implements operating procedures for food service, beverage operations, catering, marketing, and menu planning while ensuring the effective management and accountability of assigned facilities, equipment, and resources. Oversees the financial management of club operations by developing and administering annual appropriated and non-appropriated budgets, monitoring expenditures, and maintaining appropriate financial controls. Ensures operational resources, inventory, merchandise, furnishings, and equipment are properly maintained and accounted for. Addresses inventory discrepancies, initiates necessary adjustments or reports, and ensures required financial reports and management requests are completed within established deadlines. Provides leadership and oversight of employees by establishing training expectations, monitoring performance, and ensuring staff members are properly prepared to carry out their assigned responsibilities. Promotes a productive work environment and ensures employment practices are consistent with applicable equal employment opportunity requirements. Collaborates with installation leadership, Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) personnel, vendors, suppliers, and other organizational partners to coordinate club activities, communicate operational requirements, address concerns, and support the successful delivery of services and special events. Ensures assigned facilities and equipment are maintained in a safe, secure, and serviceable condition. Identifies and resolves deficiencies involving workplace safety, food sanitation, security, and facility maintenance to support compliance with applicable standards and requirements. Includes scheduling, assigning work, setting priorities, approving/disapproving leave and evaluating performance. Assigns and prioritizes work, evaluates performance, recommends awards/pay adjustments, approves/disapproves leave requests, recommends candidates for hire, supporting Equal Employment Opportunity mandates and objectives and initiates corrective and/or disciplinary actions via the appropriate channels as required. See attached Statement of Authority.
